 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani
 On The 9 th Of April, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 1194 of 2025
 Chhote Singh
 Versus
The State
Of Madhya Pradesh And Others

Appearance:
 Ms. Prachi Sharma - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Saket Udeniya - Public Prosecutor for the State.

Order 
1. This criminal appeal (third) under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed against the order dated 23.01.2025 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities) Bhind, whereby the application moved by the appellant for grant of bail under Section 483 of BNS in connection with Crime No.125/2024 registered at Police Station Malanpur,
District Bhind for the offences punishable under Sections 450, 323, 376(1), 376D of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act has been dismissed.
2.

sentences.text: Allegation against the applicant is that on hearing the shriek of the prosecutrix he entered in the room where co-accused was committing rape with her, but instead of saving her, he was laughing and thereafter went away by closing the door from outside.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8243 2 CRA-1194-2025 3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is in custody since 30.05.2024.
Second appeal of the appellant has been dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 05.11.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No.11173/2024.
Thereafter, prosecutrix, her parents and other six witnesses have been examined before the learned trial Court.
The parents of the prosecutrix turned hostile and did not support the story of prosecution at all.

Though prosecutrix has supported the story of prosecution in chief examination,
but in cross-examination she denied the allegation against present applicant.
There is no criminal history against the applicant.
He is ready and willing to comply with any condition which may be imposed by the Court.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the appellant.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Order 
1. This criminal appeal (third) under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed against the order dated 23.01.2025 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities) Bhind, whereby the application moved by the appellant for grant of bail under Section 483 of BNS in connection with Crime No.125/2024 registered at Police Station Malanpur,
District Bhind for the offences punishable under Sections 450, 323, 376(1), 376D of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act has been dismissed.
2.
Allegation against the applicant is that on hearing the shriek of the prosecutrix he entered in the room where co-accused was committing rape with her, but instead of saving her, he was laughing and thereafter went away by closing the door from outside.
He is in custody since 30.05.2024.
Thereafter, prosecutrix, her parents and other six witnesses have been examined before the learned trial Court.
The parents of the prosecutrix turned hostile and did not support the story of prosecution at all.
There is no criminal history against the applicant.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
opennyai_summary.decision:
He is ready and willing to comply with any condition which may be imposed by the Court.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case , but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this appeal is allowed by setting aside the order dated 23.01.2025 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities) Bhind, and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the appellant:-
i) The appellant will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
ii) The appellant will co-operate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;
iii) The appellant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be;
iv) The appellant will not commit any other offence or will not repeat the offence in future.
In case, if he is found involving in the offence of the same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
v) The appellant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and vi) The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
8. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
